title: Long Range Dual Motor Performance
infotainment: Android Automotive OS with Google built-in (Google Maps, Google Assistant, Google Play), 11.2-inch portrait touchscreen, 12.3-inch driver display
adasStandard: Polestar Pilot Assist (adaptive cruise + lane centering up to ~80 mph), front collision warning with automatic emergency braking (incl. pedestrian/cyclist detection), blind-spot information system with steer assist, rear cross-traffic alert with brake assist, lane-keeping aid, road sign information, driver alert control, Park Assist Pilot. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-2/specifications/, https://cars.usnews.com/cars-trucks/polestar/2
adasOptional: Surround view (360-degree) camera bundled in the standard Performance Pack trim package for MY25 (no longer a standalone option since the lineup was simplified). Source: https://recharged.com/articles/2025-polestar-2-buying-guide
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard. Conventional rear backup camera with dynamic guidelines displayed on the 11.2-inch portrait infotainment screen when reverse is selected. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-2/specifications/
sideViewCameraNotes: 360-degree surround-view camera standard on MY25 Performance Pack trim. No dedicated side-camera-on-turn-signal Honda LaneWatch-style feature. No trailer-view camera. Source: https://recharged.com/articles/2025-polestar-2-buying-guide
subscriptionFeatures: Polestar Connect connected services (live traffic, Google Maps real-time data, remote app functions) are included for the initial ownership period; renewal-pricing structure after the included term is published on the Polestar US site and varies. No subscription gate on heated seats, ADAS, or core driving features. Performance Software Upgrade is a one-time paid unlock, not a recurring subscription, and is already included on this Performance Pack trim. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/support/faq/over-the-air-updates/
drmNotes: Heavily software-defined. Core driving works offline, but Google Maps navigation, Google Assistant, OTA updates, Polestar app remote control, and connected services require cellular connectivity. Performance Software Upgrade was historically sold as a paid OTA unlock (~$1,195) on lower trims to add ~68 hp — bundled standard on the MY25 Performance Pack trim, so this trim ships with the unlock already applied. No public examples of post-sale remote feature reductions for paying owners. Sources: https://www.polestar.com/us/owning-a-polestar/ota/, https://www.currentnotesev.com/p/thoughts-on-polestar-2-software-update
killSwitchNotes: No impaired-driving kill-switch system is fitted. Polestar 2 lacks a driver-monitoring camera (the brand's Smart Eye DMS first ships on Polestar 3 and Polestar 4). The IIJA-mandated passive impairment detection rule is expected to land around 2027, post-dating this MY25 vehicle. Data unavailable: no Polestar statement on retrofit. Source: https://www.kbb.com/car-news/nhtsas-new-kill-switch-law-approaches-key-deadline/
knownIssues: Owner reports of intermittent 12V battery drain, infotainment freezes/reboots, occasional Pilot Assist dropouts. CCS1 charging port (not native NACS on MY25 — Supercharger access via $230 adapter + OTA). Source: https://www.polestar-forum.com/
recalls: Polestar 2 has had multiple NHTSA recalls across model years including high-voltage battery coolant issues (earlier MYs) and software-related items addressable via OTA. Check NHTSA VIN lookup for MY25-specific open campaigns. Source: https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls
stateIncentives: Polestar 2 is built in China and was not eligible for the federal $7,500 New Clean Vehicle Credit under post-IRA assembly/battery sourcing rules (the federal credit itself expired Sept 30, 2025). Some state incentives may apply: Colorado, Massachusetts (MOR-EV — Polestar 2 listed eligible), New Jersey, and others have historically offered $1,500-$4,000 rebates; check the buyer's state at time of purchase. Source: https://mor-ev.org/eligible-vehicles, https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/hybrids-evs/electric-cars-plug-in-hybrids-that-qualify-for-tax-credits-a7820795671/

adasStandard: Polestar Pilot Assist (adaptive cruise + lane centering), front collision warning with AEB (pedestrian/cyclist), blind-spot information with steer assist, rear cross-traffic alert with brake, lane-keeping aid, Smart Eye driver-monitoring camera, surround-view camera (360), Park Assist Pilot, head-up display. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-3/specifications/
adasOptional: Pilot Pack (Polestar 3 has most ADAS standard; Pilot Pack on lower trim levels added 360-camera and Park Assist Pilot historically — review build sheet at order). Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-3/
rearViewCameraNotes: Standard high-resolution rear backup camera with dynamic guidelines on 14.5-inch center display. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-3/specifications/
sideViewCameraNotes: 360-degree surround-view camera standard. No Honda-LaneWatch-style side-blind-spot camera. No trailer-view camera. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-3/specifications/
subscriptionFeatures: Polestar Connect connected services included for initial ownership period (live traffic, app remote functions, real-time Google Maps data); pricing for continued service post-included-term is published on the Polestar US site. No subscription gate on heated seats, ADAS, or core driving features. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/support/faq/over-the-air-updates/
drmNotes: Heavily software-defined. Google built-in (Maps, Assistant, Play), Polestar Connect app, and OTA updates all require cellular connectivity. Core driving works without internet. NVIDIA DRIVE Xavier (MY25) compute. Free OTA updates via Polestar Connect (included for the initial term). No public reports of post-sale remote feature reduction for paying owners; however the recall fixes for the 12V/HLCM and rear-view camera issues were/are partially OTA-delivered, demonstrating Polestar's ability to alter vehicle behavior remotely. Sources: https://www.polestar.com/us/owning-a-polestar/ota/
killSwitchNotes: No federal impaired-driving kill switch fitted. The Smart Eye driver-monitoring camera is present and monitors eye gaze/eyelid for distraction and drowsiness alerts, but this is not the IIJA-mandated impairment-prevention/disable feature (NHTSA rulemaking ~2027 still pending). DMS can be muted within trip but is on by default each ignition cycle. Source: https://www.polestar.com/us/polestar-3/
knownIssues: Owner-reported software/connectivity bugs including frozen screens, Bluetooth dropouts, Pilot Assist 'Driver support failure' messages, audio cutting out, and onboard AC charger failures requiring extended service stays. Source: https://recharged.com/articles/2025-polestar-3-reliability
recalls: 5 NHTSA recalls on the 2025 Polestar 3: rear-view camera may not display when shifting to reverse; panoramic glass sunroof may detach; water damage to engine-bay-to-front-bumper electrical harness connectors; missing front-bumper hood-wing bolts; 12V system fluctuations damaging the high-to-low voltage converter module. Sources: https://theevreport.com/polestar-3-electrical-harness-recall, https://recharged.com/articles/2025-polestar-3-reliability
stateIncentives: Polestar 3 was assembled in Charleston, SC (US production) plus China for some units; federal credit eligibility varied by VIN and was potentially eligible for the $7,500 federal credit on US-built VINs before Sept 30, 2025 expiry. After Sept 30, 2025, no federal credit. State incentives (MA MOR-EV, CO, NJ, CA CVRP where active) may apply per buyer state. Source: https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/hybrids-evs/electric-cars-plug-in-hybrids-that-qualify-for-tax-credits-a7820795671/
